actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository holds 3D models for eight Deep Robotics robots (Lite3, M20, M20S, X30, M20_Piper, DR02 Pro, DR02 Standard and S10) in MJCF, URDF and, where available, USD formats
The bundled models are low-resolution; high-resolution models are distributed separately
The Lite3 model is an MJCF document whose root element is <mujoco model="Lite3">
The model's compiler settings declare radian angles and autolimits
The torso is a body at 0 0 1 m with childclass robot and a freejoint named floating_base
The torso inertial has mass 5.6056 kg
The front-left leg's HipX, HipY and Knee hinges have ranges -0.523 to 0.523, -2.67 to 0.314 and 0.524 to 2.792 rad
The other three legs declare the same three joint ranges, so the model has four legs with three hinge joints each
The actuator section declares 12 motor actuators, three per leg, named <leg>_<joint>_ctrl
Every Lite3 actuator has gear 1 and ctrlrange -30 to 30
The model references STL meshes for the torso, hip, thigh and shank from its meshes directory
The model excludes contacts between the torso and each hip and between each leg's adjacent bodies
The model declares two track cameras, front_camera and side_camera
The sensor section declares framepos, framequat, framelinvel, frameangvel, velocimeter, accelerometer and gyro sensors

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element, so one ctrl sequence and tick count repeat a trajectory; the bridge takes no seed input and a reset restores the model defaults, so no seed selects a different state.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses Lite3/mjcf/Lite3.xml for the 19 qpos and 18 dof coordinates and the 12 motor ctrlranges, then treats each control as a direct joint acceleration; it computes no inertias, contacts, friction, joint limits, gear or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result

the MJCF states no option timestep (Lite3.xml:18-19 carry only compiler settings), so the 0.002 s step is MuJoCo's library default; the bridge publishes the stand-in value, and no trajectory was compared with the engine
the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture: the torso, hip, thigh and shank meshes under Lite3/mjcf/meshes are not loaded and the contacts of Lite3.xml:168-185 are not resolved
the bridge's reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults (zero qpos in the stand-in), not from the floating-base pose at Lite3.xml:48-49; the model declares no keyframe
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the step only

no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the front_camera and side_camera of Lite3.xml:148-149 and the seven sensors of Lite3.xml:187-195 are not exposed, only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is served
one package serves one device: the driver and fake use models[0], Lite3/mjcf/Lite3.xml; the clone's M20, M20S, M20_Piper, S10, X30 and two DR02 models are not served
the bundled model is a low-resolution simulation asset: no physical Lite3 is modelled or controlled and nothing here was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
